page.title: Accuracy improvement of golf swing pose estimation
page.description: Bringing golf swing pose estimation closer to practical use through targeted dataset expansion and an efficient annotation workflow.

sections.title: Goal
paragraphs: General-purpose pose estimation performs well on everyday poses. However, sport-specific movements—especially uncommon postures and occluded joints—can reduce accuracy below the level needed for practical use.
This project aims to bring golf swing pose estimation quality to a practical level.

sections.title: Difficulty
paragraphs: We began by expanding our training dataset, based on the hypothesis that the training data distribution was a root cause of the model’s accuracy issues. Our observations suggested that the model did not generalize well to sport-specific movements.

In practice, annotating human poses in video is a massive workload. We had hundreds of videos, each containing hundreds of frames. Annotating every frame was not feasible in terms of either time or cost. We needed a smarter way to address this bottleneck.

sections.title: Accomplishment
items: I worked with the team to define a more objective video filtering standard, reducing the annotation workload by approximately two-thirds.
I managed an outsourced annotation team of around 10 people to complete the work.
I established annotation workflows and practical tips for faster labeling, and refined the definitions of several joints to make the process more efficient and less prone to human error.
We annotated approximately 480,000 joints across 30,000 frames in about two weeks, at a cost of around US$3,000.

Model accuracy: Developed during the YOLOv8 era, our improved model achieves accuracy comparable to YOLO26x in 2026 when joints are visible. It still outperforms YOLO26x when the torso occludes the arms, particularly during the follow-through in down-the-line swings and the transition in face-on swings.
Model efficiency: The model remains lightweight enough to run in real time on edge devices. The computation complexity is close to YOLO nano model
The newly trained model automatically ignores distracting poses from people other than the golfer.

subsections.title: Internal workflow
paragraphs: While managing this project, I created tools and documented the workflows and lessons learned. If the company starts another round of annotation, future teams can build on this experience without spending time solving the same problems again. The documentation covers:
items: How to use the internal management tool to improve the efficiency of an outsourced annotation team.
Practical tips for making annotation faster and improving its quality.
The reasoning behind the joint definitions and the benefits of defining them this way.

subsections.title: Production
paragraphs: For production, I created and delivered:
items: A standardized data pipeline to merge existing and newly annotated datasets for model training.
An architecture for model training, inference, and Core ML conversion.
Cross-functional collaboration with the iOS team to deploy the Core ML model in the end product.
